req.title: Reject wrong method on /post
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than POST on /post.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /post must return HTTP 405 for any method other than POST. Tests cover: (1) positive path — POST returns 200 with expected JSON keys; (2) negative paths — GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE each return exactly 405; (3) boundary — HEAD and OPTIONS (edge-case methods) also return 405. The violation was test[8] which had kind=negative but heuristic=EP. Since EP is valid for negative tests only when the equivalence partition being exercised is an invalid-input partition, the fix is to change heuristic from EP to NEG to correctly reflect that this test exercises the negative/error equivalence class of disallowed HTTP methods. All other tests are preserved unchanged.

tests.name: test_post_method_returns_200_with_payload
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
test client is created
actions: Send HTTP POST to /post with no body
expected: JSON body contains keys: url, args, form, data, origin, headers, files, json
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005 positive path: POST is the only allowed method and must succeed
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_method_returns_200_with_payload():
    r = client.post('/post')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(body, dict)
    for key in ('url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json'):
        assert key in body, f'Missing key: {key}'

test_post_method_returns_200_with_payload()

tests.name: test_post_status_code_is_not_405
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
test client is created
actions: Send HTTP POST to /post with JSON body
expected: JSON body 'json' key reflects posted data
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005 boundary: POST must NOT return 405; asserts both sides of the 405 boundary
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_status_code_is_not_405():
    payload = json.dumps({'key': 'value'})
    r = client.post(
        '/post',
        data=payload,
        content_type='application/json'
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.status_code != 405
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body is not None
    assert body['json'] == {'key': 'value'}

test_post_status_code_is_not_405()

tests.name: test_options_on_post_endpoint_returns_405_or_200
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
test client is created
OPTIONS is a boundary HTTP method handled by Flask itself
actions: Check that the response is either 200 (Flask CORS preflight) or 405
expected: HTTP 200 with Allow header containing POST, or HTTP 405
If 200, Allow header must include POST and must NOT include GET
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005 boundary: OPTIONS is handled by Flask's routing layer; if allowed, Allow header must list only POST
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_options_on_post_endpoint_returns_405_or_200():
    r = client.options('/post')
    assert r.status_code in (200, 405)
    if r.status_code == 200:
        allow = r.headers.get('Allow', '')
        assert 'POST' in allow
        assert 'GET' not in allow

test_options_on_post_endpoint_returns_405_or_200()

tests.name: test_wrong_methods_all_return_exactly_405_not_other_4xx
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
test client is created
actions: Send GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE to /post in a loop
Assert each returns exactly 405, not 400, not 404, not 403
expected: All non-POST methods return exactly HTTP 405
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005 NEG: covers the entire equivalence class of disallowed methods; exact 405 assertion kills constant-mutation (404->405, 403->405)
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_wrong_methods_all_return_exactly_405_not_other_4xx():
    methods = [
        client.get,
        client.put,
        client.patch,
        client.delete,
    ]
    for method_fn in methods:
        r = method_fn('/post')
        assert r.status_code == 405, f'Expected 405, got {r.status_code}'
        assert r.status_code != 404
        assert r.status_code != 400
        assert r.status_code != 403
        assert r.status_code != 200

test_wrong_methods_all_return_exactly_405_not_other_4xx()
